Susan —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Helion’s timeline (pilot start in early Oct, procurement committee week of Sep 20) is tight but workable. I pulled together a concise onramp checklist that aligns the MAP, evaluation gating, and legal steps so your procurement team can see dependencies at a glance. Key questions before we lock dates:

- Do you require a SOC2 package and evidence before signature, or is SOC2 in-parallel OK?
- Will legal accept our standard MSA redlines (we've attached a clean + marked-up copy) or do you need a tracked-comment PDF from counsel?
- Who will sign the Order Form — procurement or a delegated BU lead?

Attached: Helion_MAP_v3.xlsx (proposed MAP with milestones), MSA_redlines_helion.pdf (redlines).

Proposed next steps:
1) We confirm MSA redline owners this week (target Aug 11).
2) Procurement aligns on acceptance criteria and security evidence (target Aug 17).
3) We publish a finalized MAP and DocuSign Order Form (target Aug 20) to enable signature in the Sep procurement window.

I’ll loop in Karthik for sequencing details and Laura for the acceptance criteria matrix.

Thanks —
Alex
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Alex —

Appreciate the summary. Quick answers:
- SOC2 evidence: we need SOC2 Type II report before contract signature for Tier-1 vendors. That said, we can accept a recent SOC2 + attestation while legal finishes up, but procurement will not OK spend without the report PDF.
- MSA redlines: our counsel prefers tracked comments in Word, but a PDF is fine for initial review. We will generate tracked-comment feedback if we escalate.
- Order Form signer: Procurement prefers the VP of Technology to sign the Order Form; finance will need a line in the PO request.

Two asks from our side: can you provide an explicit acceptance criteria spreadsheet (pass/fail gate items by test) and a minimal list of required evidence for security and data residency? Also — who will be the Redwood point person for the legal redline call?

We'll aim to complete our preliminary review by Aug 17 as you proposed.

Thanks,
Susan
Susan Walters
Head of Procurement, Helion Health

Susan — thanks, that level of specificity helps. Per your asks, attaching a concise acceptance criteria worksheet and evidence checklist in the MAP workbook (Helion_MAP_v3.xlsx). High level:

- Acceptance gates:
  * Pilot readiness (data ingest + end-to-end latency under 300ms median for key routes)
  * Quality smoke tests (prompt set pass rate >= 85% on key evals)
  * Security checklist (SOC2 pdf, encryption config, VPC peering signoff)

- Evidence we will provide: SOC2 Type II report, encryption-at-rest config screenshot, sample audit logs (anonymized), data retention policy extract, and a short runbook for incident response.

Karthik will lead the legal sequencing call and will propose a staged redline cadence that minimizes churn: legal review -> 1 consolidated comments doc -> 30-min redline sync -> final legal approval. Laura will own the acceptance criteria matrix and will share a skeleton test plan.

Proposed meeting: Aug 12, 10:00-10:45 PT for legal + procurement + product to align on sequencing. Can procurement confirm availability?

Best,
Alex

Folks —

I sketched a short sequencing checklist to reduce the back-and-forth and keep your Sep procurement window intact. Main idea: stage the legal and security evidence so procurement can run in parallel with technical evals. Summary:

1) Contract kickoff (Aug 12 sync) — attendees: Helion legal, Helion procurement, Redwood legal (me), Alex. Outcome: agree on negotiation owner, doc cadence, and SOC2 acceptance approach.

2) Security evidence delivery (Aug 13–Aug 17) — Redwood delivers SOC2 pdf + evidence bundle. Helion validates; any security gaps logged as issues (not blockers for MSA redline).

3) MSA redline exchange (Aug 13–Aug 20) — one consolidated comments doc from Helion legal on Aug 17; Redwood responds by Aug 19.

4) Order Form prep (Aug 20–Aug 24) — finance fields (pricing/compliance) locked; DocuSign draft shared Aug 24.

5) Final sign-off window (Sep 20–Sep 24) — Procurement committee meets Sep 20. If all checkpoints green, VP signs Order Form.

Notes and fallbacks: if counsel needs extended review, we propose a short canary: run DocuSign with signature authority reserved until legal clears specific clauses. That preserves procurement cadence while legal completes deep items.

I attached a one-page sequencing checklist and a suggested Agenda for Aug 12.

-Karthik
Legal & Contracts, Redwood Inference

- Please add a short column in the MAP that marks which items are approval blockers vs information-only (we need to flag SOC2 as a blocker for finance).
- DocuSign flow: procurement prefers the ability to pre-authorize the Order Form so the VP only needs to approve the final numbers. If Redwood can provide a pre-filled draft by Aug 24, procurement will circulate it internally.

We will aim to deliver a consolidated legal comments doc by Aug 17 as discussed. Michael from our security team will join the call and will want to discuss the audit-logs format and retention SLA.

See you tomorrow.

Susan
